subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: As an emerging country such as India develops, its economy typically shifts towards:
options: Manufacturing and growing service industries
Mostly subsistence farming
Reduced industrial output
Hunting and gathering
questions.explain: Industrialisation moves an economy from farming towards manufacturing and services, raising incomes and development.

options: A system ensuring producers in poorer countries get a fair, stable price
Selling goods at the lowest possible price
Trade with no rules or agreements
Banning all imports from other countries
questions.explain: Fair trade guarantees producers a fair and stable price, helping farmers in developing countries earn a reliable income.

questions.q: Why can a single indicator like GNI per capita be misleading about development?
options: It only applies to rich countries
It is always inaccurate
It measures life expectancy instead of income
It is an average and hides inequalities within a country
questions.explain: Averages such as GNI per capita hide the gap between rich and poor and say nothing about health or education.

questions.q: In the Demographic Transition Model, Stage 1 is characterised by:
options: Falling death rate and high birth rate
Low birth rate and high death rate
High birth rate and high death rate
Low birth rate and low death rate
questions.explain: Stage 1 has both high birth and death rates, so the population stays low and stable.

options: A government-owned charity
A company that operates in more than one country
A type of international aid agency
A small local business in one town
questions.explain: A TNC is a large company with operations, such as factories or offices, in several different countries.

questions.q: Which is a benefit a TNC can bring to an emerging country like India or Nigeria?
options: Reducing the country's exports
Creating jobs and bringing investment
Lowering the literacy rate
Removing all local industry
questions.explain: TNCs can create employment, bring investment and skills, and boost exports, helping economic development.

questions.q: At which stage of the Demographic Transition Model does population grow most rapidly?
options: Stage 4
Stage 1
Stage 2, when death rates fall but birth rates stay high
Stage 5
questions.explain: In Stage 2 the death rate falls (better healthcare and food) while the birth rate stays high, causing rapid population growth.

questions.q: Which of these is a physical cause of the development gap?
options: A skilled, well-educated workforce
A landlocked location or frequent natural hazards
Good trade links with neighbours
High government investment in schools
questions.explain: Physical factors such as being landlocked, having a harsh climate or suffering natural disasters can slow development.

questions.q: What does GNI per capita measure?
options: The number of births per year
The average income per person in a country
The literacy rate of adults
The total population of a country
questions.explain: GNI per capita is the gross national income divided by the population, giving the average income per person.

options: Only the amount of money a country earns
The total population of a country
The physical size of a country
The progress a country has made in economic, social and quality-of-life terms
questions.explain: Development measures how advanced a country is in terms of wealth, technology and the standard of living of its people.

questions.q: How can tourism help a developing country close the development gap?
options: It always damages the economy
It reduces the country's foreign earnings
It brings in income and creates jobs
It removes the need for any other industry
questions.explain: Tourism generates foreign income and creates jobs, which can be invested in services and infrastructure.

questions.q: What does HDI (Human Development Index) measure?
options: Only a country's income per person
The number of doctors in a country
A combination of income, education and life expectancy
Only the literacy rate
questions.explain: HDI is a composite index combining income (GNI per capita), education and life expectancy to give a fuller picture of development.
